source: Bank for International Settlements, locational banking statistics (WS_LBS_D_PUB), key Q.S.C.A.TO1.A.5J.A.<reporting country>.A.5J.N: cross-border claims, all instruments, all currencies, all counterparties, US dollars; 5A = all reporting countries
note: Cross-border claims are what banks in one country are owed by borrowers in other countries: loans, deposits and debt securities, in every currency, converted to US dollars by the BIS. A country is where the lending bank's office is, not the nationality of the bank, so a Japanese bank's London branch counts as the United Kingdom. Financial centres such as the Cayman Islands book loans for banking groups based elsewhere. The BIS counts claims on other banks and on offices of the same bank too, so this is not all credit to companies and households. Not assigned is the BIS total minus the countries it lists: it is where the BIS estimates a late reporter (in the newest quarter 0.97% of the total) and, in some older quarters, countries it did not publish separately. Source: Bank for International Settlements.
